response.reading_text: The rapid expansion of remote work has fundamentally altered the urban landscape, creating a paradoxical trend where city centres are becoming less crowded while suburban areas and rural locations see a surge in residential interest. While the initial phase of the pandemic accelerated this shift, the underlying desire for flexibility and a better work-life balance has persisted long after lockdowns ended. For many professionals, the ability to choose their own environment has become a non-negotiable requirement rather than a luxury. Consequently, traditional office models are being reimagined; companies are no longer solely focused on maximizing desk space but are instead investing in hybrid systems that allow employees to split their time between the office and home. This transition has led to a significant reduction in daily commuting, which not only saves time but also lowers carbon emissions associated with traffic congestion. However, the decentralisation of the workforce has also presented new challenges, particularly regarding team cohesion and spontaneous collaboration. The physical office, once a hub for informal networking and quick brainstorming sessions, now serves a more specific purpose: providing a dedicated space for deep work and social interaction that cannot be replicated digitally. As businesses adapt, the definition of 'productivity' is evolving, moving beyond mere output metrics to include factors such as employee well-being and sustainable commuting habits.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Remote work has completely eliminated the need for physical offices.
The shift to remote work has created complex changes in urban living and workplace dynamics.
Urban centres are currently experiencing a population increase due to new jobs.
Digital communication is now superior to face-to-face interaction for all business purposes.
questions.answer: The shift to remote work has created complex changes in urban living and workplace dynamics.

questions.question: According to the text, why has the desire for remote work persisted after the pandemic?
options: Because the government mandated it for all industries.
Because employees found it easier to work from home than in an office.
Because the flexibility and improved work-life balance it offers remain valuable.
Because technology has made it possible to work from anywhere at any time.
questions.answer: Because the flexibility and improved work-life balance it offers remain valuable.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the physical office in the modern workplace, according to the author?
options: To provide a space for deep work and focused collaboration.
To serve as a central hub for informal networking and spontaneous meetings.
To replace the need for digital communication tools entirely.
To offer a more comfortable environment for employees who dislike working at home.
questions.answer: To serve as a central hub for informal networking and spontaneous meetings.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the author's attitude towards the decentralisation of the workforce?
options: It is entirely negative and should be reversed immediately.
It is a neutral observation with no significant impact.
It is a positive development that brings challenges but offers benefits.
It is a temporary solution that will inevitably fail in the long term.
questions.answer: It is a positive development that brings challenges but offers benefits.

questions.question: What can be inferred about the future of 'productivity' in the context of this passage?
options: It will be measured solely by the number of tasks completed.
It will focus more on employee well-being and sustainable practices.
It will remain unchanged as long as output metrics are high.
It will depend entirely on the availability of high-speed internet connections.
questions.answer: It will focus more on employee well-being and sustainable practices.
